AA · T13 · timing rule (T11 with the 2-of-3 entry) · pre-registration sha256 ab1d6f4747e6 · data: APPROVED_DATA.md as of 2026-11-17

Does the 2-of-3 index switch (hold the parent when at least two of the Nifty 100, Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 weekly signals are BUY), with a fixed 50/50 sleeve and with a MAUc1-timed GOLDBEES sleeve, choose when better than chance on the four real parents' own stocks, 2014-09-01 → 2019-01-02?

2014-09-01 → 2019-01-02 · four real parents, each through its own baskets and Eikon stock prices · decisions every Friday, trades next session at OHLC4 · 10.4 bps a side · 2,000 draws per book, cost and null · every number is computed from evidence/headline/

Before you read the numbers.

Low power. 9 round trips of the in-or-out switch and 8 sleeve trades (shared by the four books) are all the evidence there is, on a window of 4.2 years (2014-09-01 → 2019-01-02). The smallest return edge detectable at 80% power against F1 (timed) is 12.5 to 20.8 pp a year; against F3 3.4 to 3.7 pp. A FAIL will mostly mean "not distinguishable from chance"; the minimum detectable edge (2.8 × the null's SD) is printed beside every FAIL below.

  • The rebuilt parent NAV is not validated. Rebuilt from the parent's baskets and Eikon prices, not validated against a published NAV before 2019-01-02. The rebuild code matches the published NAV within 0.3 pp a year over 2019-2026 (and the engine re-checks the seam on 2019), but nothing before 2019-01-02 can be checked.
  • Nine manual Eikon exports (delisted stocks, provenance unrecorded) price held stocks inside the window: held stock-sessions per parent SCMO_0003 574, SCMO_0007 123, SCMO_0010 556, SCMO_0029 122; R7 below re-runs without their returns.
  • Carried bars: SCMO_0003 0, SCMO_0007 0, SCMO_0010 3, SCMO_0029 0 in the window (a bar repeated from the previous session, kept by the project convention). The Muhurat sessions: sessions without any stock bar (2017-10-19) use the previous close as stand-in and no trade falls on them; GOLDBEES has no own bar on 2016-10-30.
  • Stock-days with a one-day move of 20% or more (listed in R7): SCMO_0003 0, SCMO_0007 0, SCMO_0010 1, SCMO_0029 0; none was checked against a second source, and price returns leave out dividends.
  • No hold-out exists. T11 ran the all-3 rule on these exact weeks, parents, prices and costs, and the 2-of-3 entry was proposed after that result; T09 ran a three-index proxy over the same weeks. Any finding is PROVISIONAL at most; every row of the weekly index and MAUc1 signals is a backfill by the production code.

The answer

On this stretch with the four real parents: the fixed-50/50 rule does not clear the pass mark against random in-or-out timing (A1 or A2 fails); the MAUc1-timed rule does not clear the pass mark against random in-or-out timing (C1 or C2 fails); the MAUc1 timing of the sleeve is not distinguishable from random gold timing (C3 or C4 fails). Each real parent is held (its own basket in force, at the listed weights) when at least two of the weekly supertrends of the Nifty 100, Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 are BUY (T11 required all three), and otherwise a sleeve of GOLDBEES and cash: 50/50 in Part A, and 80/20 when the weekly MAUc1 gold supertrend is BUY and 20/80 when it is SELL in Part B. Judged against random timings on 2014-09-01 → 2019-01-02, after 20.8 bps. A1 (return) and A2 (worst fall) of the 50/50 rule against F1 run with the 50/50 sleeve: 0 of 4 books and 0 of 4 at the 90th percentile (pre-registered pass: 3 of 4 each); F2 beside: 0 and 0. C1 and C2, the timed rule against F1 (real MAUc1 signal in every draw): 0 of 4 and 0 of 4; F2 beside: 0 and 0. C3 and C4, the gold timing against F3 (real in-or-out switch): 0 of 4 and 0 of 4; F4 beside: 0 and 0. Holm-adjusted p-values (m = 6) are in the table.

The catch: the stocks are the parents' own, but the NAV before 2019-01-02 is a rebuild that nothing can check, the window is seen and short, and there are 9 round trips and 8 sleeve trades to learn from. The 2-of-3 entry was proposed after T11's result on the same weeks (all six criteria failed with the all-3 entry); the rest of the rule, its weights and the signals were chosen after earlier results were seen. On the window starting 2015-01-02 (R3) the 50/50 rule, the timed rule and the gold timing clear the 90th percentile in 0, 0 and 0 of 4 books. Every result here is in-sample and PROVISIONAL.

What to be careful about

  • Each null randomises one timing and holds the other real. F1 and F2 move the in-or-out switch and read the real gold signal in whatever weeks they are OUT (with the sleeve fixed at 50/50 for A1 and A2); F3 and F4 keep the real switch and move the gold signal. A pass says the rule's timing beats random placement of that one ingredient, not that it beats holding the parent. Both random together is only a robustness check (R5).
  • Only C3 and C4 bear on the gold timing. A1 to C4 are T11's criteria with the 2-of-3 entry; T11's stored percentiles on the same weeks are in R4. The gold nulls move only the sleeve's split, so their spread is narrower than F1's (see the power tables).
  • Nothing is out of sample. The 2-of-3 entry was chosen after T11's result on these weeks; the rule, the 80/20 weights and MAUc1 were chosen after seeing earlier results; the window was seen in earlier studies. The all-3 rule beside it is descriptive only (section all-3 beside 2-of-3). On the window starting 2015-01-02, the 50/50 rule, the timed rule and the gold timing clear the 90th percentile in 0, 0 and 0 of 4 books.
  • The books are one market. SCMO_0007's return percentile for the timed rule against F1 is 19.9 and against F3 42.0.

The data

Each book is one of the four real parents, SCMO_0003, 0007, 0010 and 0029, run through its own baskets (D19 weights, D05 dates) and Eikon stock prices (D18, price returns, split/bonus/demerger adjusted, the Polyplex correction applied) from 2014-09-01 to 2019-01-02. The calendar is D26's. The three weekly index signals are D03's Master files (Smallcap 100 rows from 2011-11-25 only, standing rule 7). The gold signal is the weekly SIGN of MAUc1, MCX gold futures, recomputed from the start of the export (D24b). The sleeve is GOLDBEES (D09, from 2014-07-01, no parent) and cash (the LBES level, D11). Every file below is an APPROVED row of data/APPROVED_DATA.md, whose "As of" date is 2026-11-17 (the run recorded 2026-11-17). The published NAVs (D17) are opened only by the V4 regression and seam check on 2019; no price after 2019-01-02 enters a result.

Caveats, disclosed: (1) the NAV of the window is a rebuild from the parents' baskets and Eikon prices, not validated against a published series before 2019-01-02. (2) Nine manual Eikon exports for delisted stocks (provenance unrecorded) are held inside the window; HEXT and PIRAMALFIN carry export bars on every session. (3) Three carried bars in the whole window, all in one parent. (4) The Diwali Muhurat evening 2017-10-19 has no stock bars (the previous close stands in, no trade falls on it) and the Muhurat sessions 2016-10-30 and 2018-11-07 are thin; GOLDBEES has no bar on 2016-10-30. (5) Stock-days with a one-day move of 20% or more were never checked against a second source, and ordinary dividends are not in the price series. (6) The LBES file's source before 2026-08-10 is unrecorded (F-AA-D09); LIQUIDCASE cash (R2) is expected to change nothing. (7) Decisions are a backfill by the production code, and so is every MAUc1 row. (8) The 2-of-3 entry was chosen after T11's result on the same weeks (the all-3 entry, all six criteria FAIL); the rest of the rule, its weights and the signals after earlier results; T09's result on the same weeks was seen too. (9) The Smallcap 100 prices before 2011-10-03 and its signal before 2011-11-25 are not read.

One backtest, end to end (SCMO_0029, 20.8 bps, 2014-09-01 → 2019-01-02)

1. The decision. On Friday 2014-12-19 (week 16) the latest weekly rows of the three index files read Nifty 100 SELL, Midcap 100 BUY, Smallcap 100 SELL, and the latest MAUc1 row (2014-12-19) reads SELL. 1 of the three index signals is BUY, fewer than two, so the target is the sleeve, split 20% GOLDBEES / 80% cash because MAUc1 is SELL (Part A would split it 50/50); last week the book held the parent.

state(d) = IN if at least two of SIGN_Nifty100, SIGN_MC100, SIGN_SC100 are BUY (latest row dated on or before d), else OUT (T11: all three BUY) g(d) = SIGN of the latest MAUc1 row dated on or before d w(d) = 0.8 if g(d) = BUY, 0.2 if SELL IN → the parent's basket in force, at its listed weights (renormalised to sum 1); a new basket replaces it on the first session on or after its availableDate OUT → w(d) GOLDBEES + (1 − w(d)) cash (changed only when the target changes)

2. The exit trade. On the next session, 2014-12-22, at the (open+high+low+close)/4 of every instrument the book sells the parent's stocks and buys GOLDBEES and cash. Value before: 1.206955; value traded (both sides): 2.413910; cost = traded × 20.8 ÷ 2 ÷ 10,000 = 0.002510. After the trade GOLDBEES is worth 0.240889 and cash 0.963556, that is 20.00% in GOLDBEES (target 20% of the value after cost, 1.204445). The GOLDBEES fill is GOLDBEES's own de-spiked OHLC4. NAV at the close after the trade: 1.205137.

traded = Σ |target value − held value| cost = traded × cost_bps ÷ 2 ÷ 10,000 GOLDBEES value = w × (V − cost) cash value = (1 − w) × (V − cost) new units = value ÷ fill price

3. Units. Before the exit (after the previous trade, 2014-12-01) the book holds 15 stock lines (first three: AARTIDRUGS.NS 0.000823, JBMA.NS 0.001943, FINCABLES.NS 0.000310), GOLDBEES 0.00000000, LBES 0.00000000; after it (2014-12-22) 0 stock lines, GOLDBEES 0.00975614, LBES 0.00065299.

4. A gold flip (sleeve rebalance). While OUT on both sides, a change of the MAUc1 signal re-splits the sleeve; the weights otherwise drift. On Friday 2015-05-15 (week 37) MAUc1 turned BUY (the week before: SELL) while the book was OUT in both weeks, so on 2015-05-18 it sold and bought GOLDBEES and cash from their drifted values to 80% / 20% of the sleeve value after cost. 10. How one F1 draw is made. It keeps the 9 in-spells and 9 out-spells, the first state (in) and the totals (115 weeks in, 113 out), and draws every length as an integer from 2 to 30 (in) or 2 to 33 (out; each bound is the series' own: the lower is min(2, shortest spell of the state), the upper its longest spell), every allowed set of lengths equally likely. With c(m, t) the number of ways to write t weeks as m lengths in the bounds, c(0, 0) = 1 and c(m, t) = Σ over x of c(m − 1, t − x), the parts are drawn one at a time: with m parts and t weeks left, P(length = x) = c(m − 1, t − x) ÷ c(m, t). The uniform number u is rng.random() and the length is the first x whose cumulative weight exceeds u × c(m, t). In-spell parts come first, then out-spell parts, from the same generator. The real MAUc1 signal is then read in whatever weeks the draw is OUT; for A1 and A2 the same states are run with the sleeve fixed at 50/50.

allowed in-tuples c(9, 115) = 120,432,707,298 (count_table.json: 120,432,707,298) allowed out-tuples c(9, 113) = 144,224,745,588 (count_table.json: 144,224,745,588)

The first step of draw 0, in-spell 1: m = 9 parts and t = 115 weeks left, so the 29 candidate lengths 2 … 30 have weights c(8, 115 − x). u = 0.993192; u × c(9, 115) = 119,612,758,413 falls in the weight of length 30, so the first in-spell is 30 weeks.

11. How one F3 draw is made. The same sampler, with the gold series' spells: 10 BUY-spells and 9 SELL-spells, first state BUY, totals 132 weeks BUY and 96 SELL; BUY lengths are integers from 2 to 36, SELL lengths from 2 to 19 (the real series' shortest and longest spells, computed before any return was read), BUY lengths first, then SELL, from default_rng([16, 11, 6, 0]). The real in-or-out switch is kept, so the book holds the parent in exactly the rule's weeks and only the split of its sleeve moves.

12. The ranking. A1 (50/50 rule against F1 run with the 50/50 sleeve): the rule's CAGR beat 234 of 2,000 draws, tied 0, and was beaten by 1766: percentile = (234 + 0.5 × 0) ÷ 2,000 × 100 = 11.70; p-value = (1 + 1766 + 0) ÷ (2,000 + 1) = 0.8831. Against F2 with the 50/50 sleeve: percentile 17.00, p = 0.8301. C1 (timed rule against F1): beat 277, tied 0, beaten by 1723: percentile 13.85, p = 0.8616; against F2 20.00, p = 0.8001. C3 (against F3): beat 840, tied 0, beaten by 1160: percentile 42.00, p = 0.5802; against F4 42.90, p = 0.5712.

The comparators are benchmarks, not nulls. Hold the parent: the engine with the decision fixed IN (it follows every basket change). The constant mixes hold the rule's average share (50.4%, invested weeks ÷ weeks) in the parent's basket all the time and rebalance at every decision and at every basket change, with a 50/50 non-stock share and with a MAUc1-timed one; the 100% sleeves are the other end; the 50/50-sleeve rule is Part A's rule, so the gap to the timed rule is the sleeve's effect. There is no published-NAV comparator (the parents' published NAVs start on 2019-01-02). Every NAV here is rebuilt from the parent's baskets and Eikon prices, not validated against a published NAV before 2019-01-02.

The all-3 rule (T11's) beside the 2-of-3 rule, 2014-09-01 → 2019-01-02 (descriptive)

T11's rule held the parent only when all three index signals were BUY; this test's rule holds it when at least two are. Both are run by the same engine on the same prices, baskets, sleeves and costs (runs strategy_all3 and strategy_all3_fixed50; gate V4(a1) checks that they equal T11's stored runs). This comparison is descriptive: there is no null for the difference, no percentile and no pass mark (T13.md section 1 does not ask whether 2-of-3 beats all-3 in a statistical sense). The gap shows what the looser entry changed in money terms on these weeks. Rebuilt from the parent's baskets and Eikon prices, not validated against a published NAV before 2019-01-02.

The highest-return F1 draw against the rule (SCMO_0003)

The right-hand end of the SCMO_0003 F1 (timed sleeve) CAGR histogram above is draw 1621: CAGR 41.9% (end value 4.4×), against the rule's 9.5% (1.5×). It holds the parent portfolio for the same 115 weeks and switches the same number of times as the rule, but its spell lengths are its own; its sleeve reads the real MAUc1 signal in whatever weeks it is OUT. Its states are row 1621 of evidence/headline/draw_states.npz, key SCMO_0003|full|io|N4.10 (read straight from the file, no rebuild), and its curve is draw_curves_20.8.npz key SCMO_0003|F1_1621.

Returns are close to close between trade dates, before cost, and compounded within each stretch, so the stretches explain the gap between the two paths but do not add up exactly to the CAGR difference. "Right call" is the timing that was in the better of the parent portfolio and the 50/50 sleeve over the stretch (the sleeve here is the plain 50/50 one: the stretch table compares the parent portfolio with a neutral sleeve, not with the MAUc1 split). Draw 1621 is the best of 2,000 F1 draws, so it is the extreme of the null by construction, not a rival rule.

MDE = 2.8 × the SD of the draws (80% power, two-sided 5%), per null. The numbers did not exist when the pre-registration was written; its thresholds do not depend on them.

Definitions

  • Percentile: (draws worse + 0.5 × draws tied) ÷ draws × 100, ties equal within a relative 1e-12. p-value: (1 + draws at least as good) ÷ (draws + 1). Holm p: the Holm step-down adjustment of the six deciding p-values of a book.
  • CAGR: NAV_end^(252 ÷ (sessions − 1)) − 1, daily NAV, after cost. Worst fall (maximum drawdown): the most negative NAV ÷ running peak − 1.
  • The parent: the real parent's own basket in force, at its listed weights, replaced at each basket change while held. MAUc1: the weekly supertrend (period W, multiplier 2) of MCX gold futures (D24b). Gold signal g: its SIGN, BUY or SELL, from the latest weekly row dated on or before the decision date. Sleeve: while the rule is OUT, GOLDBEES and cash, 50/50 (Part A) or 80/20 when g is BUY and 20/80 when SELL (Part B), changed only when g changes.
  • F1 in-or-out N4.10 with the real gold signal (seed default_rng([16, 6, id])); F2 in-or-out N4.9 spell shuffle ([16, 3, id]); F3 gold N4.10-g with the real switch ([16, 11, 6, id]); F4 gold N4.9-g spell shuffle ([16, 11, 3, id]); F5 an F1 and an F3 draw together (robustness only). F1 and F2 are also run with the sleeve fixed at 50/50 (F1f, F2f in the tables), the nulls of A1 and A2.
  • N4.10 free-length random timing: the same number of spells of each state and the same totals of weeks in each, every length an integer between the series' own bounds for that state, uniform over all allowed ordered tuples, drawn exactly by a dynamic programme, no rejection. N4.9 spell shuffle: the real series' spells of each state reordered among themselves. All nulls start in the real series' first state.
  • Weeks versus sessions: the in-or-out nulls hold invested weeks exactly; a week has 3 to 5 sessions, so invested sessions differ by draw and are reported.
  • MDE: 2.8 × the SD of the draws' CAGR (or maximum drawdown). R3 window: 2015-01-02 → 2019-01-02.
